title: GTA6 Early Files Found in Massive 200GB GTA 5 Leak Showing Scrapped Liberty City DLC
description: A massive 200GB GTA 5 leak reveals Rockstar Games once planned a massive Liberty City DLC before scrapping it, alongside very early GTA 6 files. Read the full analysis.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Massive 200GB GTA 5 Leak Reveals Scrapped Liberty City DLC and Early GTA 6 Files

The gaming community is once again buzzing following a major leak involving Rockstar Games. According to a report by gaming media outlet Eurogamer, a nearly 200GB version of GTA 5's source code has surfaced online, shedding light on previously unknown development history and early work related to the highly anticipated GTA 6.

### The Scrapped Liberty City Expansion

Among the most significant findings within the massive 200GB data dump are traces suggesting that Rockstar Games once initiated, and subsequently scrapped, plans for a massive Liberty City DLC for GTA 5. This revelation touches upon a long-standing desire within the community for single-player expansions, a staple of the franchise in earlier eras.

While players spent years wondering why GTA 5 never received story-based expansions akin to its predecessors, the leaked source code seemingly confirms that bringing Liberty City into the GTA 5 engine was indeed considered and actively worked on at some point before being shelved due to shifting development priorities.

### Very Early GTA 6 Files Included (Unconfirmed Rumor)

In addition to the discarded DLC data, the leaked material reportedly includes very early files related to GTA 6. Given the immense anticipation surrounding Rockstar's next mainline entry, any glimpse into its formative development stages naturally captures the attention of industry watchers.

However, it is important to contextualize these findings. Because the information stems from an unverified and unauthorized leak, details regarding these early files should be viewed with caution. Industry analysts note that preliminary source code and early planning documents rarely represent the final vision of a finished game.

### Editor's Take

This 200GB leak offers a fascinating, albeit unauthorized, look behind the curtain at Rockstar Games' internal development decisions. While the revelation of a cancelled Liberty City DLC sparks a sense of what could have been, it also highlights the difficult choices developers make behind closed doors. For GTA 6 fans, patience remains key as we wait for official updates directly from the studio.
